lines.text: Approving a technical institution takes many hands, many documents, and many deadlines.
This prototype keeps every one of them visible, from the first form to the final decision.

chapters.title: The public portal
chapters.purpose: Schedules and rule changes, open to everyone

lines.text: Before anyone signs in, the public portal shows this cycle's schedule, and every rule change.
Text can be made larger.
The whole site switches to Hindi.
And a high-contrast mode helps anyone with low vision.
Accessibility is not an extra screen. It is built into every page.

chapters.title: A college files
chapters.purpose: Catch mistakes while the form is being filled

lines.text: Applications are long, and a mistake found months later can cost a college the whole cycle.
ABC Engineering College starts a new application. The header shows the cycle, and the exact rules version it is filing under.
Here, the built-up area is entered as larger than the land itself.
Check my entries flags it straight away, as advice, not a block. The college corrects the figure.
But a missing critical document does block submission, and the message names it: the land lease.
With the lease attached, the application goes in.
Submitted, with its own application number.
Problems are caught at the desk, not months later.

chapters.title: Assigned, with reasons
chapters.purpose: Who handles a case, and why

lines.text: In most offices, who handles a case, and why, is invisible.
The new case is already in Priya's Action Center.
And it says why: she is the portfolio officer for this college, with her workload and the rules version that applies.
Every assignment explains itself.

chapters.title: Return and reply
chapters.purpose: A clock that is fair to both sides

lines.text: Delays are often blamed on the wrong side.
Priya finds the lease covers only two years. She returns the application, naming the document and the reason.
The case turns amber. The clock is paused, because the next move is the college's.
The college replies with a three-year lease.
And the case goes straight back to Priya, with the days that were left, not a fresh deadline.
The clock is fair to both sides.
Overdue work tends to be forgotten, quietly.
For the demo, the administrator moves the simulated date forward by twenty days.
The deadline engine has escalated the unscheduled visit to the manager, Kumar. Exactly once. And his dashboard shows why.
Nothing slips through unnoticed.
When an officer is away, their queue usually just stops.
Kumar records a week of medical leave for Arjun. His open tasks are released, and reassigned, each with a reason.
Kumar can also move work by hand. The system recommends who has capacity, and his choice is recorded.
Work follows capacity, not chance.
Approval is not the end. The conditions attached to it have to be met.
Ravi schedules the expert visit, with a committee proposed by the system.
The committee files its report.
And the competent authority approves, with a condition: a fire no-objection certificate within ninety days.
Eighty-five days later, after reminders at thirty, fifteen and seven days, the college uploads the certificate. Priya verifies it.
And the case closes, on its own.
From application to closure, one traceable thread.

chapters.title: Rules change every year
chapters.purpose: Change that is previewed, approved and announced

lines.text: Rules change every year. Sudden changes surprise colleges, and break systems.
A rules editor drafts an amendment: a new required document, and a longer application window.
Applying the new document to cases already filed is refused. A tighter rule can only apply to new applications.
Before anything is published, the impact preview shows exactly who would be affected.
Then a different person, the rules approver, reviews it and publishes it. Nobody can approve their own change.
And the college sees the change the next time it signs in.
Every change is previewed, approved by two people, and announced.

chapters.title: Trust
chapters.purpose: A record that cannot be quietly changed

lines.text: An audit log that can be edited proves nothing.
Every action is chained by hash. Verify integrity, and every row checks out.
Now, with a demo tool, one row is changed directly in the database.
Verification points to the exact broken row.
And when an officer opens a case outside their region, access is refused, and logged.
Tamper-evident, and scoped to every role.
The AICTE Demo Website. A prototype on synthetic data, for Smart India Hackathon twenty twenty-six. Try it live, at the link on screen.
